statements.status_notes: Per the upstream advisory (GHSA-jqcq-xjh3-6g23), DataRow.Decode only panics when decoding messages from 'a malicious or compromised PostgreSQL server' because a negative field length travels from the server wire protocol into pgproto3. harbor-core only connects to a PostgreSQL server the Harbor operator controls (the bundled harbor-db component or an operator-supplied DSN). The attacker cannot reach pgproto3.DataRow.Decode without first compromising that backend server, at which point they already have direct database access that supersedes this DoS primitive. pgproto3/v2 is archived upstream with no fix on the v2 branch; migration to pgx/v5 must happen in Harbor itself.

pgproto3/v2 is a transitive dependency via pgx/v4. The standalone pgproto3/v2 module is archived with no fixed v2 release available. The vulnerability is resolved in pgx/v5's internal pgproto3, but migrating Telegraf's pgx/v4 dependency chain to pgx/v5 is a major upstream change.
